Dataset / source: ESDC 2024 Building a Barrier-Free Workplace employee survey (12,069 responses)
Coverage: ESDC, 2024; 12,069 employees, including employees with disabilities
Key fields relevant to DTA: Confusing or delayed workplace accommodations: 51% of employees with disabilities versus 21% without; onsite environment accessible: 34% versus 65%; comfortable discussing accessibility needs with supervisors: 69% versus 86%.
Barrier signal: 30 percentage-point gap in confusing or delayed accommodation processes; local ESDC survey, not 2024 PSES and not national.
Best-practice signal: Explicit comparative outcomes; a 2024 baseline that can be tracked against later ESDC DTA process reforms.

Dataset / source: ESDC 2025 Employees with Disabilities Network consultation survey (414 responses)
Key fields relevant to DTA: 25% comfortable discussing accessibility needs with supervisors; 30% felt no progress in accommodation processes; 35% reported little progress in clear support guidance.
Barrier signal: Low confidence among participants, but network-member survey is self-selected and not equivalent to the ESDC-wide 2024 sample or PSES.
Best-practice signal: Consultation recommends clear DTA accountability, a simpler process, manager training and a centre of expertise; subsequent outcomes are not yet demonstrated.

Dataset / source: Canadian Heritage Bob Fern Centre accommodation case statistics (Jan–Oct 2024)
Coverage: Canadian Heritage; 196 requests addressed and 121 completed January–October 2024
Key fields relevant to DTA: Among reported closures: 28% in under 10 days; 25% in 11–21 days; 34% in 21–60 days; 10% in 2–6 months; 4% over 6 months. Percentages are rounded and reported as closure bands.
Barrier signal: 121 of 196 requests were completed in the reporting period; closure timing is not time to an effective accommodation and categories total 101% due to rounding.
Best-practice signal: Named centralized intake and service centre; unusually detailed published case-volume and time-band evidence; case mix is not disclosed.

Dataset / source: Health Canada accessibility feedback 2025 (employee and public submissions)
Coverage: Health Canada 2025 progress report, 41 feedback submissions (31 employees, 10 public)
Key fields relevant to DTA: Four submissions tagged to the employment area, which includes accommodation and hiring. Category totals are not counts of accommodation requests.
Barrier signal: Feedback counts do not establish employee DTA effectiveness, prevalence, or accommodation request volumes.
Best-practice signal: Published feedback breakdown by area, a visible response pathway and manager training launched in fall 2025; accommodation process review reported.

Dataset / source: Privy Council Office Accessibility Plan 2026–2028: central funding and intake
Key fields relevant to DTA: Reports a centralized accessibility fund and a centralized employee accommodation request process. Disability employment equity representation reported as 9.1% in September 2025, compared with 3.2% in March 2020.
Barrier signal: No comparable time to effective accommodation or DTA satisfaction result in the cited executive summary; increased representation is not a DTA result.
Best-practice signal: Central funding and centralized request intake are concrete structural features worth evaluating with outcomes.

Dataset / source: Public Service Commission 2023 staffing and assessment accommodation barriers
Coverage: 2023 Staffing and Non-Partisanship Survey results discussed in PSC 2026 action plan
Key fields relevant to DTA: 12% of employees with disabilities versus 5% of all federal public servants reported avoiding a promotion process for fear that existing accommodations would not be accepted in a new role; only 56% of employees with disabilities who needed staffing/second-language assessment accommodation requested it.
Barrier signal: Evidence of potential chilling effects and lost opportunities; assessment accommodations differ from workplace accommodation requests.
Best-practice signal: Supports proactive offers, portability of measures, clear information and a Passport across recruitment and staffing transitions.

Dataset / source: Federal Digital Technologies Accessibility Regulations and transition direction (2025–2027)
Coverage: Government of Canada guidance issued following December 2025 regulatory changes and March 2026 CIO direction
Key fields relevant to DTA: The former Standard on Web Accessibility was rescinded effective March 2026; amended regulations require new or updated federal web pages to meet CAN/ASC EN 301 549 on December 5, 2027. Departments must maintain interim WCAG 2.0 compliance under CIO direction.
Barrier signal: Web accessibility is not a direct workplace DTA case outcome; applies to regulated organizations under stated timelines, not to this independent website as an official GC site.
Best-practice signal: Provides a stronger digital-design benchmark and a way to track whether employee-facing accommodation tools become accessible.

Dataset / source: PPSC employee accessibility and accommodation survey: outcomes by request status (2022)
Coverage: Public Prosecution Service of Canada National Accessibility Plan 2022–2025; 49 accommodation request responses
Key fields relevant to DTA: Of 49 requests: 34 accepted (69.39%); 2 denied (4.08%); 11 ongoing (22.45%); 2 received a measure other than what was requested (4.08%). Of 50 satisfaction answers, 48% very satisfied and 28% somewhat satisfied.
Barrier signal: Small, self-selected employee survey and earlier period; category outcomes do not establish employer-wide case decision rates or timeliness, and do not align with 2024 PSES Q86.
Best-practice signal: Rare published example of full/partial/ongoing/denied status breakdown for employee accommodation needs; provides a model for what other organizations could report.

Dataset / source: 2024 PSES new accessibility stress and career-barrier questions (Q44d, Q44e, Q73o, Q73p)
Coverage: Federal public service, 2024 PSES by organization and disability status
Key fields relevant to DTA: Q44d and Q44e measure accessibility and accommodation issues adversely affecting career progress; Q73o and Q73p ask whether accessibility and accommodation issues cause work-related stress. These question families are not fully in the current organization comparison CSV.
Barrier signal: The 2024 official concordance lists Q73o and Q73p as new rather than historic comparable questions; negative and positive summary calculations for question 73 changed since 2022. Do not infer trends from unlike formulations.
Best-practice signal: Strong opportunity to expand the existing organizational profiles with barrier and stress outcomes and their original denominators; source is public, detailed results have not yet been ingested into the website's 92-organization comparison.

Dataset / source: ESDC 2024 PSES accommodation-related stress indicator and 2025 accessibility target
Coverage: ESDC 2025-2028 Accessibility Plan using 2024 PSES Q73p as of April 1, 2025
Key fields relevant to DTA: 19% of ESDC employees with disabilities reported accommodation issues causing work-related stress to a very large extent in the PSES 2024 result cited in the plan; ESDC lists a baseline of 15% and a target of 3%.
Barrier signal: This measure concerns the very-large-extent stress response, not the proportion of requests denied, and it should not be presented as a national or cross-year equivalent without checking the change in PSES questions.
Best-practice signal: A transparent organization-specific outcome indicator linked to a departmental accessibility target and a proposed intake and case-management improvement by 2027.
